Verify an artefact
Certification authority for software correctness

Verification as evidence, not verification as opinion.

AxiomCode checks Lean 4 artefacts with a real toolchain — the Lean kernel is the only judge — and issues signed, revocable certificates that bind the artefact hash, the verdict, and the toolchain. Don’t trust our AI — verify our proof.

Scope, stated at the point of claim: Lean 4 artefacts only, today. A PASSED verdict means the artefact’s proofs checked under the stated toolchain — not that the software does what you intended. What verification does not prove.

Try it — live

One loop: artefact in, evidence out

This is the real service, not a recording. Paste your own API key and run the starter artefact, or replace it with your own Lean 4. The first 10 cases on a key are the trial: real verdicts and usage records, no certificate.

1 · Artefact in

Your key goes only to api.axiom-code.com, over HTTPS; this page never stores it. No key yet? Request one by email — keys are free. Prefer the dedicated page? The same loop runs at /verify/.

→

2 · Evidence out

The verdict appears here — PASSED or FAILED, decided by the Lean kernel, with the artefact hash and the usage record. A run that ends before a verdict (payment required, timeout, refusal, failed queued job) is a NO VERDICT error outcome, never a verdict. On the trial, no certificate is attached — by design.

Driving an agent instead? The same call is one POST over REST, or seven tools over hosted MCP. First time here: the first-verification tutorial walks the whole loop.

The seal

What a certificate binds

A certificate is a signed record, not a badge image. Anyone can check it — paste it into the public checker and the signature, the validity window, and the revocation state are verified in your browser against our published CA keys.

{
  "artifact_hash": "sha256:9f2c…e41a",
  "verified": true,
  "toolchain": "lean4-4.9.1 / axiomcode-0.3.0",
  "issuer": "AxiomCode CA",
  "serial": "AC-2026-000417",
  "issued": "2026-09-26", "expires": "2026-12-25",
  "signature": "ed25519:…"
}
Read the fields, not the logo. The hash binds the exact bytes that were checked; the toolchain names what checked them; the serial is how a certificate is revoked if the toolchain is ever found wrong. A certificate without these fields is a picture, not evidence.
Verdicts

Two verdicts — and one non-verdict

Verdicts are boolean. Anything that ends a run before a verdict exists is an error outcome with its own name, so a refusal can never be mistaken for a result.

OutcomeWhat it meansCertificate?
PASSEDThe artefact compiled and every proof checked under the stated toolchain.Yes — on paid verifications. Trial runs return the verdict and usage record only.
FAILEDThe artefact was checked and did not pass: a proof failed, or the artefact was rejected by the engine’s rules.Yes — on paid verifications. A FAILED certificate is evidence too: it records that the check ran and what it found.
NO VERDICTNo verdict exists: payment required (402), engine timeout (504), concurrency, rate, or size refusal, or a queued job that failed. The run ended before a verdict.Never. Nothing was decided, so nothing is certified.

The full taxonomy — every status code and what it does to your balance — is in the verdicts & errors reference.

Questions

Asked often

What exactly does a PASSED verdict claim?

That the submitted artefact compiled under the stated Lean toolchain and its proofs checked — the kernel accepted them. It does not claim the specification says what you meant, that the deployed system matches the artefact, or anything about code that was not submitted. The bounds are stated on every certificate and in what verification proves.

Why does the trial withhold the certificate?

Because the certificate is the product: our signature staked on a verdict, with the revocation and record-keeping duties that follow. Trial runs give you the verdict and the usage record so you can judge the engine; the signature is issued inside a paid relationship.

Can I check a certificate without an account?

Yes. The checker verifies the signature in your browser against the published CA keys, and the revocation list is public. Checking never requires trust in this website.

Which languages are supported?

Lean 4, today. Smart-contract verification is in design and the offline verifier is not built — both are labelled as such on the status page, not implied here.

Stated plainly

No external third-party audit of AxiomCode has been performed. The assurance case rests on the release gate, the soak, and the public record — read the practice page for exactly what that does and does not cover.

Found an error on this site or in the service? Report it on GitHub Issues — user-initiated only; this site carries no telemetry and attaches nothing you did not choose to send.
